newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures fall, but off early lows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures fall, but off early lows.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended lower on Wednesday, although early losses were curbed by trade house buying late in the day after seeing the firmer CBOT Project A trade, traders said.
The market started the day lower, tracking a Chicago market pushed down by a wet weather in the U.S. Midwest.
The benchmark July 1998 contract was down 250 yen at 14,440 yen per tonne. Volume was estimated at 75,228 lots.

"If there is rain this weekend as expected, the benchmark should probe the downside at 13,000 yen," one analyst at a commodity broker said. The lower Tokyo corn prices relative to the Chicago market encouraged some trade house buying late in the day.

Another trader said further falls could be limited due to reports that Sparks Companies, the private Memphis-based firm, pegged U.S. corn production at 9.47 billion bushels, below the USDA's July outlook.

The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.56 per bushel at 0839 GMT, against $2.54-1/4 at Tuesday's close. The spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.62 per bushel at 0839 GMT, against $7.63 at Tuesday's close.
